summary: 81-year-old nursing-home resident with Parkinson's and chronic constipation, 2 days of massive distension; AXR coffee-bean sign, CT whirl without ischaemia.

inputs.hpi: Nursing-home resident with Parkinson's disease and chronic constipation on laxatives. 2 days of rapidly increasing abdominal distension, no flatus or stool, mild colicky lower abdominal pain, vomited once. Similar smaller episode a year ago that settled.

exam.abdomen: Massive tympanic distension, mild diffuse tenderness, no guarding, no peritonism. Empty rectum.

imaging.name: Abdominal X-ray
imaging.result: Massively dilated inverted-U loop of sigmoid colon arising from the pelvis ('coffee bean' sign).

imaging.name: CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast
imaging.result: Sigmoid volvulus with a mesenteric whirl sign. Normal bowel wall enhancement, no pneumatosis, no free gas or fluid.

inputs.socialHistory: Nursing-home resident, mobilises with a frame.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Sigmoid volvulus
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Sigmoid volvulus without clinical or CT signs of ischaemia or perforation — endoscopic decompression (flexible sigmoidoscopy, flatus tube), then consider sigmoid resection during the same admission.

socratesAnswers.associated: Distension, no flatus or stool (constipation), vomited once

mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: Web: PANE has no volvulus disease node, so it can never appear in the PANE top 3 (bowel obstruction, adhesive SBO, inguinal/femoral hernia). Symptom inference ranks sigmoid volvulus #2.

emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: Web: adaptiveTriage: 'priority_24_48h' (score 27: age ≥70, vomiting). 'Massive distension' and 'no flatus or stool' are not red-flag phrases ('unable to pass gas/stool' is).
emergencyLevel.proposedFix: Add obstruction red-flag phrases to RULES ('no flatus', 'not passed wind', 'massive/increasing distension') and a volvulus term.

mustInclude.note: First-line treatment without peritonitis or ischaemia; avoids an emergency laparotomy in a frail 81-year-old.
mustInclude.knownGapNote: Web: No endoscopic decompression step in any management output; the lbo_volvulus plan prefix is only a heading ('Sigmoid/Caecal Volvulus — Management:') followed by bowel-obstruction steps. Decompression appears only in the dx-variant urgency note.
mustInclude.proposedFix: Give lbo_volvulus a real plan prefix: sigmoid — endoscopic detorsion + flatus tube if no peritonitis/ischaemia, then sigmoid colectomy in the same admission; caecal — right hemicolectomy; gangrene/peritonitis — Hartmann's. Split into sigmoid and caecal variants.

mustInclude.note: Recurrence after decompression alone is high; sigmoid resection in the same admission if fit.
mustInclude.knownGapNote: Web: No sigmoid colectomy after decompression.
Web: No potassium replacement despite K 3.2.

guideline.name: ASCRS clinical practice guidelines — colonic volvulus and acute colonic pseudo-obstruction
guideline.section: Sigmoid volvulus: endoscopic detorsion without peritonitis/ischaemia, then sigmoid colectomy during the same admission; emergency resection for gangrene/perforation; caecal volvulus: operative management, endoscopic reduction not recommended
guideline.citation: Alavi K, Poylin V, Davids JS, et al. The American Society of Colon and Rectal Surgeons clinical practice guidelines for the management of colonic volvulus and acute colonic pseudo-obstruction. Dis Colon Rectum. 2021;64:1046–57.

guideline.name: WSES consensus guidelines — sigmoid volvulus management
guideline.section: Endoscopic decompression when no peritonitis/ischaemia; emergency surgery (Hartmann's) for gangrene, perforation or failed decompression; elective sigmoidectomy after decompression
guideline.citation: Tian BWCA, Vigutto G, Tan E, et al. WSES consensus guidelines on sigmoid volvulus management. World J Emerg Surg. 2023;18:34.

rationale: Base case for sigmoid volvulus: endoscopic decompression when there is no peritonitis or ischaemia, then sigmoid resection in the same admission if fit.
